xmldoc.short_description: Offset from UTC, in seconds, of a time zone at given serial date numbers.

param_input_item.param_description: a numeric array: serial date numbers (see datenum).
a string: time zone name (for example 'Europe/Paris', 'UTC', 'local', '+05:30' or a POSIX TZ rule).
a string: folder of the time zone database to use. An empty value keeps the current setting.
a string: 'local' (default) when dn holds wall-clock times of tz, 'utc' when dn holds UTC instants.

param_output_item.param_description: a double array of the same size as dn: offset from UTC in seconds, daylight saving time included.

description.p: timezoneoffset returns, for each serial date number of dn, the offset in seconds between the time zone tz and UTC at that date. The offset includes daylight saving time when it applies.
It is a low-level function used by datetime, tzoffset and the time zone conversions. Most scripts should use tzoffset on a datetime instead.

The names 'UTC', 'GMT' and 'Z' (any case) mean UTC, 'local' means the time zone of the operating system, and a fixed offset can be given as '+HH:MM' or '-HH:MM'. Other names are searched in the time zone database. When no database is set, a short list of common zones and POSIX TZ rules such as 'EST5EDT,M3.2.0/2,M11.1.0/2' are still accepted.
When dataPath is given, it becomes the database folder of all the time zone functions for the rest of the session. Nelson ships a database in [modulepath('time'), '/resources/tzdata'].
Non-finite values of dn (NaN, Inf) give an offset of 0. An unknown time zone raises an error.

example_item.example_item_description: Offsets of Paris in winter and in summer.
